content.text: A string is a sequence of characters treated as a single object in java.
it lives in heap, not stack
once a string object is created, it cannot be changed.
every method .toUpperCase() or .replace() doesn't touch the original, it creates and returns a brand new string object.
java maintains a special area in Heap called as string pool.
when you write "hello", java checks if "hello" already exists in pool. If yes, it reuses the same object instead of creating new one.
-> checks if they're same object in memory
-> checks if the content is same
